Subject: Jurisdictional runbook: EU residency + APAC standby (renewal coordination)

Amelia —

Quick note as we prepare Novagene's upcoming renewal: your contract comes up Oct 1, and you've indicated interest in adding an APAC standby topology plus tightening EU residency guarantees. To make the renewal smooth, I've drafted a short operational runbook and a pricing amendment that reflect:

- EU primary tenancy (data at rest and processing within EU region)
- APAC warm-standby node for burst traffic and DR (no persistent storage in APAC)
- Cross-region failover procedure with RTO/RPO targets and manual/auto failover options
- Suggested term change: 12->24 months with staged capacity top-ups to reduce unit cost

I'm attaching the runbook + a draft amendment. Can you confirm the following from your side so we can align legal and ops before the renewal call next week?

1) Is Novagene comfortable with APAC standby being cold-storage-only and only serving tokenized inference during bursts?
2) Do you prefer automated failover (we can provide SLA for automated) or manual failover with runbook verification?
3) Any additional compliance evidence needed (SCCs, dataflow diagrams, SOC artifact) beyond what we provided last cycle?

If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-minute run-through with your security and infra leads.

Thanks —
Rachel

--
Rachel Kim

Hi Rachel —

Thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. A few quick answers and notes from ops/legal:

1) APAC standby: Novagene's compliance team is OK with warm/cold standby as long as we maintain proof that no EU PII is stored or processed in APAC except transient KV cache used for inference and explicitly encrypted under our KMS.
2) Failover mode: prefer manual first (we need a runbook and an ops drill) and then move to automated after a successful DR exercise — can we contract for a staged automation milestone?
3) Compliance artifacts: we will need updated dataflow diagrams showing the APAC standby path, plus an attestation that the APAC node will not hold backups of EU datasets. SOC artifacts we already have are fine, but if there are additional export controls or new SCC updates, we'll flag them.

We're gathering the infra folks for a 30-min call on Wed (their availability is 10:00-12:00 UTC). Can you send a calendar invite? Also looping in Legal (legal@novagene.com) to start required amendments.

Best,
Amelia

Thanks for the quick turnaround, Amelia — 

Staged automation milestone is doable. I've updated the runbook to include a 3-phase path:

Phase A: Manual failover only; quarterly DR drills; APAC node sits in warm-standby (no persisted EU backups)
Phase B: Timeboxed automation trial after 2 successful drills; 30-day monitoring/stabilization window
Phase C: Full automated failover with rollback hooks and audit logging (optional, premium SLA)

On pricing: Ben, Monica — I attached a proposed amendment with two options:
- Option 1 (12->24 mo term, 15% uplift for APAC standby commitment, per-token price reduced by 8%)
- Option 2 (24 mo term, 25% capacity commit uplift, per-token price reduced by 18% + included 2 DR drills/year)

Amelia — could you confirm which option Novagene prefers so I can hand to Legal and prepare the DocuSign? If you'd like, we can present both on the renewal call and request a signed SoW amendment for the chosen option.

Proposed call: Wed 2026-08-25 11:00 UTC (30 mins) — I'll send the calendar invite now.

Rachel

Quick note from our infra lead: we prefer Option 2 (24 mo term with higher commit + included DR drills). Two items to confirm before we sign:

1) Data residency SLA: We need explicit language that confirms (a) no persistent EU customer datasets will be replicated to APAC, and (b) any transient KV cache in APAC will be encrypted under our customer-managed KMS (we will provide the key).
2) Audit window: Novagene requires quarterly access to runbook execution logs for the first 12 months after cutover; can you include log retention for 12 months (or a supported export) in the amendment?

If those two items are in the amendment, Legal will push for speed on our side. Look forward to the call.
